## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (two Suggestions and 41 inconclusive checklist items; no Critical or Important finding)

The PR is ready to merge: no reviewer and no checklist item found a defect at or above the Important threshold, and all 16 acceptance criteria were itemized and checked.

Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings below the threshold and INCONCLUSIVE checklist items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (2)

<details><summary>2 items</summary>

1. The module docstring of `tests/unit/test_sql_runner_cleanup.py` (lines 6–10, rewritten by this diff) says the outer `finally:` cleanup guards a secondary exception from `cursor.close()` / `conn.close()` when a SELECT raises. At head the outer `finally:` of `MySQLRunner._run_sql_blocking` only calls `conn.close()`, and the SELECT path never closes its streaming `SSDictCursor`; the only guarded `cursor.close()` is on the write path. The test it introduces and `docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md` describe this correctly. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: test-module docstring; no mechanism is under discussion and changing the sentence changes no output; git grep of the head view for 'shadow the primary error' finds only the docstring itself; the test file is not published or printed -->
2. The URL-scheme rule now lives in four places that apply different tests: `DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme` in `src/sqllens/config.py` (lines 109–125) accepts `mysql`, `mysql+…` and `sqlite…`, while `build_sql_runner` in `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py`, `probe_database` in `src/sqllens/preflight.py` and `sqlglot_dialect_for_url` in `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` each re-parse the raw string and accept any scheme starting with `mysql` (so `mysqlx://` passes them). `DatabaseConfig.dialect` also does not lowercase, so `MySQL+pymysql://…` passes the validator but yields dialect `MySQL`. Behavior is correct today because every config path runs the validator first and the one `dialect` consumer lowercases; the suggestion is to carry a normalized engine on the type instead of re-classifying the string downstream. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>
